name: tracing-beam
title: Tracing Beam
description: A long-form reading column of photo posts wrapped by a thin left-hand rule. As the page scrolls, a cyan-to-violet glow and a small dot travel down the rule to mark progress.
use: A long article or changelog wants a quiet progress cue running alongside the text.
avoid: You need an obvious progress bar at the top, or content has no left margin to spare.
a11y: The beam hides itself under reduced-motion and the SVG is aria-hidden, but the demo's photos all use empty alt text. (keyboard: n-a, labels: partial, reduced motion: respected)
looks: A narrow dark reading column of stacked posts, each with a small solid badge, a bold white heading, a wide rounded mountain photo and a paragraph of grey text. Down the far left runs a fine vertical rule with a zig-zag kink near the top and a small dot marker.
behaves: Scrolling sends a short cyan-to-violet gradient sliding down the left rule and drags a dot along with it, both eased through a stiff spring so they lag slightly. The top marker flips from green to white once scrolling begins.
customise: Articles go in as children and className pads the column. The zig-zag path, gradient stops and spring settings are fixed, while the beam height is measured from the content.
weight: light: One SVG path whose gradient and dot positions a scroll spring updates.
